result.report: The strongest route is Route 0, which is a single-step process with a direct literature precedent and passes all validation checks. Routes 1 and 4 are supported but rely on similar, not identical, precedents, which may affect predictability. Route 2 and 3 require further review due to predicted unintended products. The main risk is that routes without identical precedents may not proceed as expected, and predicted products must be verified. Chemists should prioritize Route 0 and confirm the alignment of predicted products with the target.

applicability.note: max_train_similarity measures structural novelty only. Calibration on the held-out test set found no relationship between it and prediction error (Pearson -0.074, permutation p=0.44), so a familiar molecule is NOT thereby a reliable prediction. For expected error use prediction_interval, whose empirical_coverage was measured on held-out data.

model_performance.note: Held-out scaffold-split metrics. The prediction should be read as roughly +/- 0.99 log10(mol/L).

prediction_interval.note: Nominal 90% interval; MEASURED coverage on the held-out test set is 81% (95% CI 73%-88%, n=113). Coverage falls short of nominal because the scaffold split puts calibration and test in different scaffold distributions, violating the exchangeability conformal assumes. Coverage is marginal across the test distribution, NOT a molecule-specific confidence for this compound.

limitations: Route scores rank candidates by the signals available; they are not yield or feasibility probabilities.
AiZynthFinder templates come from USPTO patents (to ~2019); it recovers known chemistry and will not invent new reactions.
'In stock' means present in the ZINC stock file - not priced, and not necessarily available at scale.
'No precedent' means absent from the indexed ORD/USPTO data, not unknown to chemistry.
ReactionT5 is a learned model; agreement is supporting evidence, not proof.
Nothing here has been run in a lab.

The most serious weakness in route 1 is the lack of identical literature precedents, which may affect predictability. Route 2 requires review due to ReactionT5 predicting an unintended product, even though it has a literature precedent. Route 3 also needs review because ReactionT5 predicts an incorrect product and has only similar, not identical, precedents. A chemist should check first whether the predicted product from ReactionT5 aligns with the target, and verify the availability and reactivity of starting materials.
